title: Factorized regime codes over shared Koopman eigenmodes
hypothesis: A shared orthogonal modal basis plus compact regime codes over eigenvalues recovers held-out stable Koopman dynamics with better complete bytes and transition compute than independent dense operators, while preserving stability under extrapolation audits.
physical_object: one shared orthogonal eigenbasis Q and a diagonal latent transition for each regime
mirror_coordinate: lambda(a,b)=lambda0 + a*d1 + b*d2, represented per mode

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed on exact native spectral-factor alias or any stability/quality gate miss.

controls: shared mean eigenvalues without regime code
pass_gate: Heldout horizon-48 nRMSE <=0.02, max spectral radius <1 for all registered regimes, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent dense operators, and strict frontier gain over native diagonal/spectral controls.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific value for exact native spectral alias, instability, quality miss, storage miss, or no native-control frontier improvement.

compute.active_MACs: dense shared input map plus dense Q decode plus D modal multiplies for factorized codes; dense transition for independent operator bank
compute.wall_time: small CPU synthetic rollout; not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic stable diagonal latent systems and known nonlinear observation conjugacy; no trained S4 or Koopman eigenvalue learning claim.
Regime factors are known and charged.
Extrapolation audit evaluates the registered factor grid only; out-of-range codes are reported separately and are not counted as valid regimes.
Native diagonal/eigenvalue-table and native spectral-factor controls are required.
